claims.text: The proposed coating consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The starting multilayer has uniform initial lattice parameters.
The starting multilayer has typical short-range order.
Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading is governed by evolving lattice distortion at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Interfacial lattice distortion causes a transition away from conventional primary dislocation slip.
Interfacial lattice distortion activates non-basal 〈c+a〉 slip in the proposed FCC/BCC multilayers.
Interfacial lattice distortion activates twin-bridging in the proposed multilayers.
Sustained loading causes strain to accumulate preferentially at the interfaces.
Changing interface chemistry through targeted alloying can alter the ease of lattice distortion.
In transformative HEAs, the c/a ratio of HCP epsilon martensite changes with processing and tensile deformation.
Sustained loading progressively changes local lattice parameters or effective lattice-parameter ratios at FCC/BCC interfaces.
The altered local lattice environment lowers the energy barrier for secondary slip.
A lower-than-ideal c/a ratio promotes non-basal pyramidal 〈c+a〉 slip in HCP epsilon martensite of transformative HEAs.
A lower-than-ideal c/a ratio promotes deformation twinning in HCP epsilon martensite of transformative HEAs.
Secondary slip and twin-bridging provide additional pathways that accommodate plastic strain beyond primary slip.
Interfaces that promote lattice distortion will produce earlier and more prevalent secondary slip and twinning than standard interfaces.
Interfaces engineered to resist lattice distortion will delay or suppress secondary slip and twin-bridging under otherwise identical loading.
The unmodified-interface baseline deforms predominantly by conventional primary dislocation slip with minimal secondary-mode activation.
The proposed effect is restricted to nanoscale multilayers under sub-yield sustained loading.
The proposed effect may cease to apply at substantially larger layer thicknesses or when phase transformations or extensive thermal recovery occur.

contradictions.description: The stated material contains only FCC and BCC layers, and the conditions exclude phase transformation, yet the proposed secondary mechanism is non-basal 〈c+a〉 slip and the mediator is framed through c/a-ratio evolution. Those concepts apply to an HCP phase in the cited evidence; no HCP phase or transformation producing one is included in the proposed system.
